passage:
Aparna: hey. did i do something? you bit my head off when i asked about the trip
Usha: ugh. no. sorry
Usha: i hadn't eaten since morning. lab ran over and i skipped lunch
Aparna: ok but it kind of stung. i was only asking if you'd booked the tickets
Usha: i know. it wasn't about you. i was starving and everything felt like an attack
Aparna: fair. i've been there
Aparna: honestly i went home thinking you didn't want me on the trip anymore
Usha: noooo. i really do want you there
Usha: can we sort the tickets tomorrow after lunch? like actually after lunch
Aparna: deal. i'll bring samosas just in case
Usha: you're the best 🙏

qa.q: What had Aparna asked about?
qa.a: If Usha had booked the tickets.

qa.q: What was Aparna worried about after being snapped at?
qa.a: Aparna felt stung and worried that Usha no longer wanted Aparna on the trip.

qa.q: What do they agree to, and why is it a good plan?
qa.a: To sort the tickets tomorrow after lunch, so hunger is out of the way before they return to the real question.

qa.q: How did the moment look from Usha's side?
qa.a: Usha was starving after skipping lunch, so everything felt like an attack; the snap was about hunger, not Aparna.

grounding: Shows a friend snapped at by a hungry friend taking it personally, and both agreeing to eat first and revisit the real issue later.

passage: By late afternoon at the Hampi temple fair, old school friends Sangeeta and Naveen had been selling bangles since dawn without a break. When Sangeeta miscounted change for a customer, Naveen snapped, "Can't you do one simple thing right?" Her face went hot. She almost dropped the cash box and walked to the bus stand. Then she noticed his hands trembling as he tied a bundle, and remembered neither of them had eaten since the morning idlis. "Naveen. Food first. Then you can shout if you still want to." He opened his mouth, closed it and nodded. Over hot mirchi bajji from the next stall, his shoulders dropped. "Sorry. I was horrible." Later they sorted out the real problem: one of them would handle the cash box, the other the customers.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta and Naveen sell at the fair?
qa.a: Bangles.

qa.q: What was Sangeeta feeling right after Naveen snapped?
qa.a: She felt hurt and humiliated; her face went hot and she almost walked off to the bus stand.

qa.q: What choice kept the argument from growing, and why?
qa.a: Sangeeta suggested food first; once both had eaten, Naveen could apologise and they could sort out the cash box calmly.

qa.q: How might the afternoon have felt for Naveen before they ate?
qa.a: He was likely shaky and on edge from hunger, which made a small mistake feel like a big one.

grounding: Illustrates a friend snapped at after a long day without food, and both pausing to eat before sorting out the real issue.

passage:
Saturday night
Kalyani snapped at me today, and I spent three hours sulking about it. We'd been shifting her stuff to the new PG since morning, no breakfast, no lunch, just boxes. Around four I asked where the kettle should go, and she said, "Can you not ask me one more stupid question?" I put the kettle down and went quiet. I was sure she'd been secretly fed up with me for months.
Then at six we finally got vada pav from the stall downstairs. Halfway through, she looked at me and said, "I was vile earlier. I hadn't eaten all day." Honestly, neither had I, and I'd been ready to end a four-year friendship over a kettle.
Note to self: food first, feelings after. We're talking about splitting the move costs tomorrow, after lunch.
Eshaan

qa.q: What did Eshaan ask about before Kalyani snapped?
qa.a: Where the kettle should go.

qa.q: What did Eshaan feel after the snap?
qa.a: Eshaan felt hurt and took it personally, sulking for hours and imagining Kalyani had been fed up for months.

qa.q: What is Eshaan's lesson for next time?
qa.a: Food first, feelings after: eat, then return to the real issue, which is why the costs talk is set for after lunch.

qa.q: How does Kalyani see her snap once she has eaten?
qa.a: She sees it came from hunger, calls herself vile, and apologises.

grounding: Shows a friend snapped at after a long day without food taking it personally, then both eating first and returning to the real issue later.

passage: By three in the afternoon, the temple festival stall in Pala had sold two hundred plates of kappa, and not one had reached Jomon or Deepika. When Jomon stacked the clean plates the wrong way, Deepika snapped, "Do you ever listen? Just go, I'll do it myself." Jomon stood there holding the plates, face hot, thinking of every time she had teased him this year. Maybe she really was sick of him. Then Chechi from the next stall pushed two bowls into their hands. "You two haven't eaten since morning. Sit." They ate in silence on upturned crates. Deepika wiped her mouth and sighed. "Sorry. I turn into a crocodile when I'm hungry." Jomon laughed, relieved. "Me too, apparently. So, the plates. Tell me how you want them, slowly this time."

qa.q: How many plates of kappa had the stall sold by three?
qa.a: Two hundred plates.

qa.q: What was Jomon feeling after Deepika snapped?
qa.a: Jomon felt hurt and embarrassed, face hot, and began to worry Deepika was sick of him.

qa.q: What helped them sort out the plates properly?
qa.a: Pausing to eat first, then coming back to the real issue slowly, once neither was hungry.

qa.q: How does Deepika see her own snap once she has eaten?
qa.a: She realises it came from hunger and apologises, joking that she turns into a crocodile.

grounding: Shows a friend snapped at after a long day without food taking it personally, and both pausing to eat before revisiting the real issue.

passage: By six in the evening, Mina and Abebe had been walking round Lisbon for seven hours with only coffee. When Mina suggested one more museum, Abebe snapped, 'Do you ever stop planning everything?' Mina went silent, cheeks hot. So that's what he really thinks of me, she thought. They walked to the tram stop without a word. Then Mina noticed Abebe's hands shaking slightly as he checked the map. 'When did you last eat?' she asked. 'Breakfast,' he admitted. They found a bakery and shared custard tarts and soup on a bench. Halfway through, Abebe said, 'I'm sorry. That was the hunger talking. Your plans made this trip.' They agreed to talk about the schedule tomorrow.

qa.q: What did Mina and Abebe share on the bench?
qa.a: Custard tarts and soup.

qa.q: What did Mina feel when Abebe snapped about planning?
qa.a: She felt hurt and embarrassed, taking it personally as what he really thought of her.

qa.q: What helped them pause before the argument grew?
qa.a: Mina noticed the shaking hands and asked when he last ate; they ate first and left the schedule talk for tomorrow.

qa.q: How did Abebe see the moment after eating?
qa.a: He felt sorry, recognising that hunger had done the talking, and he valued Mina's plans after all.

grounding: A friend snapped at after a long day without food takes it personally until they eat first and revisit the issue later.
